planting.note: Plant container or balled-and-burlapped trees in spring or fall in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; this precocious strain of the historic Galissoniensis selection is grown specifically because it begins flowering on much younger wood than a typical seedling tree.

directions: Galissoniensis Praecox arose as an early-flowering strain of the older European Galissoniensis selection of Southern magnolia, and European nurseries have long distinguished it from its parent specifically because young plants begin setting bloom years before an ordinary seedling tree would flower. Aside from that precocious bud-set, it grows into the same dense, pyramidal, full-size evergreen tree as Galissoniensis, carrying glossy dark leaves backed in russet-brown felting. Because its main appeal is an early and dependable flower display rather than a reduced mature size, give it the same generous footprint as a standard Southern magnolia rather than treating it as a compact form. Grow it in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil, where its earlier bloom habit lets a young specimen start contributing flowers to the garden well ahead of most other named Southern magnolia selections.
sources: Trees and Shrubs Online (International Dendrology Society)
